input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now reuses one statistics dict across all calls by clearing and writing into the shared wrapped_f.statistics object, so concurrent calls from different threads mutate the same dict.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same @retry-decorated function at once. Mechanism: each call's copy._local.statistics points at the same dict that another call's stats.clear() just emptied and is still filling, whereas before each call got its own fresh dict. Impact: attempt counts and statistics seen inside a call's retry hooks or returned via the shared dict can be corrupted or mixed between threads.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is cleared and reused for every call. Concurrent calls from different threads then clear and overwrite each other's data and see corrupted, mixed statistics. It omits the async case, but the faulty operation and the way it fails are identical.
